discovery: Conformal symmetry and the exact solution of two-dimensional critical phenomena (conformal field theory)

nominees.name: John Cardy
nominees.affiliation: University of Oxford, UK, and University of California, Berkeley, USA

subfield: Statistical physics / theoretical condensed matter and quantum field theory
motivation: Polyakov first saw that critical fluctuations are invariant under conformal transformations. With Belavin and Zamolodchikov he showed in 1984 that in two dimensions the infinite conformal symmetry fixes critical exponents and correlation functions exactly, and Zamolodchikov's c-theorem gave an ordering of renormalization-group flows. Cardy turned this framework into a working tool for real statistical systems: finite-size scaling, boundary critical behaviour, crossing formulae for percolation and the modular-invariance constraints. Together these ideas made conformal field theory the universal language of phase transitions. They are tested in experiments on two-dimensional magnets, adsorbed films, quantum Hall edges and entanglement in quantum matter, and they also underlie today's numerical conformal bootstrap, which has set the 3D Ising exponents to record precision. It is a very simple question, what symmetry does a critical point have, with an answer of enormous depth and reach across physics.
